question: A replica's pub/sub subscriber disconnects for a few seconds. Which invalidations are lost, and how does cache-kit recover?
answer_hinglish:
Redis pub/sub fire-and-forget hai. Message publish ke waqt jo subscriber connected nahi tha, usse woh message kabhi nahi milega -- Redis queue nahi karta. Toh disconnect ke dauraan doosre replicas ke saare `set` / `delete` invalidations is replica ke liye lost hain, aur iska L1 purani values serve karta rahega.

cache-kit ki mitigations, order mein:

(1) Re-subscribe par poora L1 clear. Kyunki pata nahi kaunse messages miss hue, har L1 entry suspect hai. Clear ke baad L1 Redis se refill hota hai (sasta), DB se nahi. `l1.clear()` running loads ko bhi detach karta hai, toh reconnect se pehle padhi value koi load nahi likhega. Event `resubscribed`, counter `resubscribes`.

(2) Timing ka detail jo real bug ban sakta tha: ioredis reconnect par `ready` emit karta hai apna re-SUBSCRIBE bhejne se PEHLE (ioredis 5.4.1 ke `event_handler.js` se padha gaya). Agar `ready` par L1 clear karte, toh clear aur actual subscribe ke beech ek gap rehta jisme message miss ho sakta hai aur L1 mein purani value phir aa sakti hai. Isliye `ioredisSubscriber` har `ready` par khud `SUBSCRIBE` bhejta hai aur `onResubscribed` tabhi call karta hai jab Redis CONFIRM kare. Mutation X17 (ready par call) caught.

(3) Jo koi client nahi dekh sakta: half-open connection jo abhi dead detect nahi hua. Wahan sirf L1 TTL bound hai -- isliye 'keep it short' jab replicas data share karte hain.

Tested: fake Redis mein disconnected subscriber `set` miss karta hai aur reconnect tak purana serve karta hai; real Redis par `CLIENT KILL` se subscriber connection kill -> reconnect -> L1 cleared -> naye invalidations phir aate hain.
why_needed: Pub/sub invalidation ka sabse common production failure silent message loss hai. Bina recovery ke ek replica ghanton purana data de sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: WhatsApp group jisme message history nahi: phone band tha toh beech ke announcements gaye. Wapas online aate hi samjhdaari yeh hai ki apni saari purani notes phaad do aur notice board (Redis) se phir padho.
how_it_works: `ioredisSubscriber.subscribe`: `subscribed` flag; `ready` handler `if (!subscribed) return; sub.subscribe(channel).then(onResubscribed, () => {})`. `TwoLevelCache.onResubscribed`: `l1.clear(); resubscribes++; emit({ type: "resubscribed" })`. Pehla `ready` (initial subscribe se pehle) ignore hota hai.
in_this_project: `src/two-level.ts` ke `L2Subscriber` interface comment aur `ioredisSubscriber` comment poori reasoning dete hain. `test/adapters.test.ts`: 'a ready before the first subscribe completed is ignored; after a reconnect, onResubscribed runs only once Redis CONFIRMED the new SUBSCRIBE'. `test/two-level.test.ts`: 'a subscriber that was disconnected MISSES messages'. `test/redis-l2.test.ts`: 'the subscriber connection is killed'. Mutations X10, X17, X18 caught.
advantages: Lost messages ka conservative fix: sab clear
Refill Redis se, DB se nahi
ioredis ki timing quirk handle aur tested
disadvantages: Har reconnect par poora L1 cold (flapping connection par baar baar)
Half-open connection sirf TTL se bounded
Pub/sub durable nahi
common_mistakes: `ready` event ko 'listening again' maan lena
Subscriber aur commands ek hi connection par (RESP2 mein subscriber mode sirf (UN)SUBSCRIBE / PING / QUIT)
L1 TTL ghanton ka rakhna
follow_up_questions: Redis Streams se yeh problem kaise solve hogi?
Flapping connection par L1 clear ka cost kaise kam karoge?
Half-open connection ko jaldi detect kaise karoge?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Clear-all simple aur correct hai par blunt -- ek message ke liye poora L1. Durable log (Streams) precise hota, par har replica ka consumer offset bookkeeping maangta (PLAN ne isliye reject kiya).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Flapping subscriber -> baar baar L1 clear -> Redis read load spike. Half-open TCP -> koi reconnect nahi, koi clear nahi, TTL tak stale. Re-SUBSCRIBE fail -> agle reconnect tak koi onResubscribed nahi.
advanced.alternatives: RESP3 CLIENT TRACKING (server-pushed invalidations, NOT implemented), Redis Streams (NOT implemented), TCP keepalive / PING health checks for faster detection.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Zyada replicas par ek Redis failover sab subscribers ko ek saath reconnect karata hai -> sab L1 ek saath clear -> Redis par read burst.
advanced.production_improvements: `resubscribes` par alert, subscriber connection par keepalive, L1 TTL ko tolerated staleness ke barabar rakhna.

question: A loader hangs forever and ignores its AbortSignal. What happens to that key in cache-kit, and how do you prevent it?
answer_hinglish:
Yeh README 'Known and NOT changed' mein documented failure hai. Single flight ka matlab hai ek key ka ek hi load chalta hai, aur baaki callers usi ko join karte hain. Agar woh load kabhi settle hi na ho (DB connection atak gaya, koi promise kabhi resolve nahi hua), toh:

- Jo callers bina `signal` ke aaye, woh hamesha ke liye wait karte rahenge -- unke liye flight kabhi khatam nahi hoti. Signal-less caller 'never leaves', aur load ko zinda rakhta hai.
- Signal wale callers abort karke nikal jaate hain (unke signal ke reason ke saath reject). Agar SAARE waiters chale gaye, toh load ka signal abort hota hai aur flight detach -- agla caller naya load shuru karta hai. Par agar loader signal ignore karta hai, toh purana loader background mein phir bhi atka rahega (resource leak), bas cache use bhool jaata hai.
- Background refresh ke liye aur bura: refresh cache ko permanent waiter ginta hai, toh woh kabhi abort nahi hota. Us key ka koi naya refresh shuru nahi hoga, aur grace khatam hone ke baad har caller usi stuck refresh ko join karega.

Fix library mein nahi, loader mein hai: loader ke andar timeout lagao. README seedha `projects/18-resilience` ka `TimeoutPolicy` suggest karta hai. Aur load ka `signal` DB driver / fetch ko pass karo taaki abort sach mein kaam kare. Express helper request ke disconnect signal ko `getOrLoad` mein deta hai, toh HTTP clients chale jaayen toh load abort ho sakta hai -- par sirf tab jab loader signal maane.

Tombstone ke saath bhi link hai: slow load `tombstoneMs` se lamba chala toh delete ke baad purani value wapas likh sakta hai. Timeout dono problems ka ek hi ilaaj hai.
why_needed: Single flight ek dhaar wali talwar hai: ek achha load sab ko bachata hai, ek atka load sab ko atkaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek counter par ek hi clerk saare same-type requests handle karta hai. Agar woh clerk lunch par chala gaya aur wapas nahi aaya, toh line mein khade sab log khade hi rahenge -- jab tak koi supervisor (timeout) usse hata ke naya clerk na lagaye.
how_it_works: `wait(key, flight, signal)`: `waiters++`; signal nahi toh seedha `flight.promise`. Signal abort par `leave()`: `waiters--`; zero hue aur settled nahi toh `flights.delete(key)` aur `controller.abort(reason)` + `load-abort` event. Refresh `waiters: 1` se shuru hota hai, toh kabhi zero nahi.
in_this_project: `test/load.test.ts`: 'ALL waiters abort: the load's signal is aborted, nothing is written, and the next call starts a fresh load', 'a caller without a signal keeps the load alive when every signalled caller leaves'. `test/swr.test.ts`: 'a caller that joins the refresh and aborts does NOT abort the refresh'. `projects/18-resilience/src/timeout.ts` mein timeout policy hai.

Sab chale jaayen toh load abort aur key free
Behaviour documented, chhupa nahi
disadvantages: Library khud koi load timeout nahi lagati
Signal ignore karne wala loader leak karta hai
Stuck refresh us key ke saare future refreshes rok deta hai

Bina signal ke getOrLoad call karna (worker / cron mein)

question: The database is down. What does cache-kit return for fresh keys, stale keys and keys that are not cached?
answer_hinglish:
Teen tarah ki keys, teen alag behaviour -- aur yeh sab code se seedha nikalta hai.

Fresh keys (TTL ke andar): normal hit. Loader chalta hi nahi, DB down hone se koi fark nahi. Users ko kuch pata nahi chalta jab tak TTL khatam na ho.

Stale keys (TTL ke baad, `staleMs` grace ke andar, sirf `getOrLoad`): purani value turant milti hai aur ek background refresh chalta hai. Refresh fail -> `refresh-error` event, `refreshErrors` +1, aur stale entry WAISE HI rehti hai. Agla stale read phir refresh try karta hai -- koi backoff nahi (README 'Known': hot stale key DB ko ek ke baad ek refresh bhejti hai jab tak grace khatam na ho). Grace khatam -> key plain miss.

Not cached keys (ya grace ke baad): `getOrLoad` loader chalata hai, loader fail karta hai, aur sab waiting callers ko wahi error milta hai. Error cache NAHI hota -- agla call phir loader chalata hai. Concurrent callers phir bhi single flight mein ek hi load share karte hain, toh ek key par ek waqt mein ek hi failing query. HTTP helper mein yeh `next(err)` (Express) ya Nest ka exception layer hai -- test: pehli request 503 / 500, DB theek hone par agli request 200 'miss'.

Two-level ke saath ek extra layer: L1 miss par Redis padha jaata hai. Agar doosre replica ne value pehle Redis mein rakhi thi, toh DB down hone par bhi Redis hit milta hai (PTTL tak). Negative entries (cached 'not found') bhi apni negative TTL tak chalti rehti hain.

Kyun errors cache nahi: README -- error aksar transient hota hai (timeout, restart), aur use cache karna 50 ms ke blip ko poore error TTL ka outage bana deta.
why_needed: 'DB down hone par app kya karegi' har design review ka sawaal hai. Cache ka jawab key ki state par depend karta hai, aur woh clearly pata hona chahiye.
real_world_analogy: Bijli gayi: fridge mein jo taaza hai (fresh) woh khao; jo thoda purana hai (stale) woh bhi chalega jab tak kharab na ho; jo hai hi nahi uske liye dukaan jaana padega -- aur dukaan band hai toh khaali haath.
how_it_works: `startLoad` ka catch: flight current ho toh `flights.delete(key)` (not cached), abort nahi hua toh `loadErrors++` (+ `refreshErrors++` refresh par) aur event, phir `throw error`. Stale path `getOrLoad` mein `startLoad(..., true)` -- caller ko value pehle hi mil chuki, refresh ka rejection `flight.promise.catch(() => {})` se handled.
in_this_project: `test/swr.test.ts`: 'keeps serving the stale value until the grace ends, reports refresh-error, and the next stale read retries', 'a failed refresh does not reject the stale reader'. `test/load.test.ts`: 'an error is shared by every waiter, is NOT cached, and the next call loads again'. `test/express-helper.test.ts`: 'a producer error is NOT cached'. Mutations F2 (error cached) aur R11 (failed refresh drops entry) caught.

question: Why did cache-kit choose SET NX plus tombstones instead of a Lua compare-and-set with version keys or a delayed double delete?
answer_hinglish:
Problem yaad karo: replica B ka load-ke-baad wala Redis write, A ke naye `set` ke baad pahunch ke usse overwrite kar deta tha. Teen known solutions the, PLAN mein teeno compare hue.

Delayed double delete: update ke baad delete, thoda `sleep`, phir dobara delete. Rejected: 'a sleep, still a window'. Sleep kitna? Agar B ka write sleep ke baad pahunche toh phir bhi purana. Aur har write path ab latency ya ek background timer le jaata hai.

Lua compare-and-set with version keys: har key ke saath ek version (ya DB ka `updated_at`), aur Lua script 'tabhi likho jab mera version Redis wale se naya ho'. Yeh sabse precise hai -- order kuch bhi ho, naya version jeetega. Rejected: 'more moving parts, a version per key'. Loader ko version return karna padta (DB row se), set ko version chahiye, aur Lua script ko maintain / test karna.

SET NX + tombstone (chuna gaya): rule simple -- load se aaya write kabhi overwrite nahi karta, sirf khaali key bharta hai. Explicit `set` overwrite karta hai (woh newer hai). `delete` key ko khaali nahi chhodta, ek `TOMBSTONE` likhta hai `tombstoneMs` ke liye, taaki late load ka NX bhi refuse ho. Koi script nahi, koi version nahi, ek Redis command.

Iski keemat honest: (1) 'First writer wins' for loads -- do replicas ke loads mein jo pehle likhe woh TTL tak rahega, chahe doosra naya ho (dono load the, isliye usually same data). (2) Tombstone window: load `tombstoneMs` se slow ho toh purana wapas. (3) Corrupt value ke liye exception: `onlyIfAbsent = false`, warna woh hamesha atak jaati.

Evidence: real-Redis race test 20 rounds, chaar runs mein NX 6 / 14 / 17 / 11 baar refuse hua, Redis ne hamesha A ki value rakhi.
why_needed: Distributed systems mein 'kaunsa write jeetega' ka sawaal har shared store mein aata hai. Senior engineer se expected hai ki woh options ka cost aur guarantee dono bataye.
real_world_analogy: Parking slot: version-CAS matlab har gaadi par ticket time, aur naya ticket purane ko hata sakta hai. NX matlab 'slot khaali hai tabhi park karo'. Tombstone matlab khaali kiya slot par 10 second ke liye 'reserved' cone -- taaki koi purani gaadi jaldi se wapas na ghus jaaye.
how_it_works: `writeBehind(key, value, ttl, onlyIfAbsent)` -> `redis.set(prefix + key, text, redisTtl(ttl), onlyIfAbsent)`; adapter NX par `client.set(key, value, "PX", ttlMs, "NX")`. Reply `null` = refused (`l2WritesSkipped`). `set` aur `delete` `onlyIfAbsent = false`. `readL2` tombstone ko miss maanta hai.
in_this_project: PLAN.md stage 2 decision: 'Writes after a load are SET NX, delete writes a tombstone ... Recommended over a Lua compare-and-set with version keys (more moving parts, a version per key) and over delayed double delete (a sleep, still a window).' README 'Why SET NX and tombstones'. Tests: dono RACE tests (fake, held messages), real 20-round race, 'a tombstone lasts tombstoneMs', 'an explicit set() overwrites a tombstone'.

Loader / DB se version maangne ki zaroorat nahi
Bring-your-own client ke liye interface chhota rehta hai
disadvantages: Load writes ke beech first-writer-wins
Tombstone window (slow loads)
Version-CAS jitna precise nahi

Corrupt values ke liye bhi NX (hamesha atak jaayengi)

question: cache-kit invalidates over Redis pub/sub. How would RESP3 client tracking or Redis Streams change the design, and why were they not used?
answer_hinglish:
Teeno ka goal ek hai: ek replica ne key badli toh baaki replicas ka L1 copy hate. Fark guarantee aur cost mein hai.

Pub/sub (jo bana hai): `set` / `delete` ke baad `PUBLISH prefix+invalidate [instanceId, key]`. Simple, har client support karta hai. Kamzori: fire-and-forget -- disconnected subscriber messages kho deta hai. cache-kit ise reconnect par poora L1 clear karke aur chhote L1 TTL se handle karta hai. Ek aur cost: app ko har write par khud publish karna yaad rakhna padta hai, aur jo write cache-kit ke bahar se Redis mein hua (koi script) uska koi invalidation nahi.

RESP3 client-side caching (`CLIENT TRACKING`): Redis khud yaad rakhta hai ki kis client ne kaunsi key padhi, aur jab woh key badle toh server us client ko invalidation PUSH karta hai. Fayda: invalidation automatic hai -- koi bhi Redis write (kahin se bhi) trigger karta hai, app ko publish nahi karna. README: yeh 'would replace the pub/sub channel with server-pushed invalidations'. Kyun nahi: RESP3 chahiye aur client jo support kare (PLAN), aur cache-kit ka L1 TTL / grace / negative logic Redis tracking ke model se map karna padta. NOT implemented.

Redis Streams: invalidations ek durable log mein (`XADD`). Reconnect hone par replica apne last-seen ID se replay kar sakta hai -- koi message lost nahi, toh 'clear all L1' ki zaroorat nahi. Kyun nahi: PLAN -- 'durable but needs consumer bookkeeping per replica' (har replica ka offset, stream trimming, naya replica kahan se shuru kare). NOT implemented.

Mera take: jab tak L1 TTL seconds mein hai, pub/sub + clear-on-resubscribe kaafi hai. Agar L1 TTL lamba chahiye ya ek bhi lost invalidation unacceptable hai, Streams pehla upgrade hai.
why_needed: Invalidation channel ka choice hi decide karta hai ki staleness kitni bounded hai. Interviewer dekhna chahta hai ki tum Redis ke alag primitives ki guarantees jaante ho.
real_world_analogy: Pub/sub = loudspeaker announcement (jo nahi suna, gaya). Streams = notice register (baad mein aake padh lo). Client tracking = society secretary jo khud yaad rakhta hai kisne kaunsi cheez maangi thi aur usi ko phone karta hai jab woh badle.
how_it_works: Abhi: `invalidateOthers` -> `redis.publish(channel, JSON.stringify([this.id, key]))`; `onMessage` parse, apna id ignore, `l1.delete(key)`. `L2Subscriber.subscribe(channel, onMessage, onResubscribed)` interface hai -- Streams ya tracking ke liye ek naya adapter isi shape mein `onMessage` / `onResubscribed` call kar sakta hai (design-level observation, built nahi).
in_this_project: README 'NOT implemented': 'RESP3 client-side caching (CLIENT TRACKING), which would replace the pub/sub channel with server-pushed invalidations; Redis Streams instead of pub/sub (a durable log a reconnecting replica could replay)'. PLAN stage 2: 'Recommended over Redis Streams (durable but needs consumer bookkeeping per replica) and RESP3 client tracking (needs RESP3 and a client that supports it)'.

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Pub/sub: stateless, simple, lossy. Streams: durable, par per-replica offset aur trimming policy. Tracking: automatic aur precise, par protocol / client dependency aur L1 semantics ka mismatch.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Pub/sub: disconnect = lost messages (clear-all se mitigated). Streams: consumer bahut peeche -> trimmed entries -> phir bhi clear-all fallback chahiye. Tracking: tracking table full / connection reset -> Redis 'flush all' type invalidation bhejta hai, client ko sab drop karna padta hai.
advanced.alternatives: CDC se invalidation (DB-driven), Kafka topic, ya sirf chhota TTL bina kisi channel ke.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Pub/sub har message har subscriber ko -- O(replicas) per write; write-heavy keys par yeh channel bhari hoga. Streams mein bhi har replica padhta hai, par apni speed se. Tracking per-key interest rakhti hai, toh sirf relevant clients ko jaata hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Streams adapter `L2Subscriber` interface ke peeche (not built), invalidation latency ka metric (publish se receive tak -- abhi measure nahi hota).

question: Why is TwoLevelCache a wrapper around LruCache instead of an `l2` option inside LruCache, and why does the Redis read run inside the L1 load?
answer_hinglish:
PLAN ka decision: 'TwoLevelCache wraps an LruCache instead of LruCache growing an l2 option'. Do reasons.

Pehla, sync vs async. `LruCache` ke `get`, `set`, `delete`, `peek`, `has` synchronous hain -- O(1), koi await nahi. Redis async hai: `set` / `delete` ko Redis ka jawab aur publish await karna hai, aur result `Promise<boolean>` hai. Agar `l2` option LruCache mein hota, toh ya to har method async banta (L1-only users bhi promise ka cost dete) ya do API mix hoti. Wrapper mein L1 sync rehta hai aur L2 ki async duniya alag class mein.

Doosra, reuse. Redis read L1 ke LOAD ke andar chalta hai: `TwoLevelCache.getOrLoad` = `l1.getOrLoad(key, (signal, context) => this.loadThrough(...))`. Matlab L1 ka loader hi 'Redis padho, nahi mila toh asli loader' hai. Isse stage 1 aur 2 ke saare features free mein Redis par lag jaate hain: single flight (50 concurrent misses ek replica par = 1 Redis read + max 1 loader call, tested), stale-while-revalidate (refresh bhi pehle Redis padhta hai), negative caching (Redis hit ki value bhi `isNegative` se classify), abort (sab callers Redis read ke dauraan chale gaye toh loader shuru hi nahi -- `signal.throwIfAborted()`), aur load versions (`isCurrent()`).

Yeh possible hua stage 2 ke load context se -- `ttlMs` (loader set kar sakta hai: Redis hit ka L1 copy `min(PTTL, call TTL)` paata hai), `refresh`, `isCurrent()`. PLAN: 'TwoLevelCache is built on these three' aur 'Recommended over special-casing Redis inside LruCache'. Generic hook, Redis-specific nahi -- HTTP `max-age` jaise use cases ke liye bhi wahi.

Keemat: L1 ko seedha (`l1.set`) chhu ke Redis bypass kiya ja sakta hai -- `l1` public field hai. Aur do classes ke stats alag hain (`l1.stats()` aur `stats()`).
why_needed: 'Feature add karo ya compose karo' har library design ka core sawaal hai. Yahan composition ne zero duplicate concurrency code ke saath L2 diya.
real_world_analogy: Ek achhi dukaan (L1) jo apna counter system rakhti hai; godown (Redis) ek alag supplier hai jise dukaan ka 'stock mangao' process (loader) call karta hai. Dukaan ka process badalna nahi pada -- bas supplier pehle check hota hai, factory baad mein.
how_it_works: `getOrLoad(key, loader, options)` -> `this.l1.getOrLoad(key, (signal, context) => this.loadThrough(key, loader, signal, context), options)`. `loadThrough`: `readL2` hit -> `context.ttlMs = min(...)` aur return (L1 store karega); miss -> `signal.throwIfAborted()` -> asli `loader(signal, context)` -> `isCurrent()` ho toh `writeBehind`. `set`/`delete` L1 ke sync methods + Redis await.
in_this_project: `src/two-level.ts` ka `getOrLoad` comment: 'The Redis read runs INSIDE the L1 load, so 100 concurrent misses on one replica cost one Redis read, not 100.' `src/cache.ts` mein `LoadContext` aur `loadedTtl` / `defaultTtlMs` getters TwoLevelCache ke liye. Tests: '50 concurrent misses on one replica: ONE Redis read and ONE loader call', 'a refresh reads L2 first', 'every caller leaving during the Redis read: the loader is not started'. Mutation X15 isi abort check ka hai.

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Composition: kam code, L1 unchanged, model test L1 par hi valid rehta hai. Integration: ek class, ek stats, par sync/async mix aur L1-only users par cost.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Koi app code `l1.set` seedha kare toh Redis aur doosre replicas ko pata nahi -- silent divergence. Redis read slow ho toh woh L1 flight ka hissa hai, toh joiners bhi utna wait karte hain (l2TimeoutMs tak).
advanced.alternatives: LruCache mein pluggable async 'backing store' option; ya ek generic multi-tier cache (L1..Ln) -- zyada general par zyada complex.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Per replica single flight Redis reads ko bounded rakhta hai -- replicas x hot keys, requests x keys nahi. 100 replicas par Redis read load = 100 per key per TTL.
advanced.production_improvements: `l1` ko read-only expose karna ya docs mein warning, combined stats helper, aur Redis read latency metric (abhi measure nahi).
